case.question: How many UART ports does the module have?

result.question: How many UART ports does the module have?
result.answer: The C16QS module provides three sets of UART interfaces [HW-v5.3-p033-2]. These include the UART0 serial port, which is used as the debug UART [HW-v5.3-p033-3], the UART1 serial port [HW-v5.3-p034-2], and the UART2 serial port, which is used to obtain GNSS NMEA data [HW-v5.3-p035-1].

result.question: How do I put the EVK into flight mode?
result.answer: To enable Flight mode on the Cavli C16QS EVK, you must use Jumper 9 (JMP 9), which is designated for enabling Flight mode (W_Disable) [EVK-v1.1-p013-1]. Additionally, the module hardware features a W_DISABLE# pin (Pin 18) used to put the module into Flight mode and disable RF transmission [HW-v5.3-p051-2].

case.question: Which port gives out the GNSS location data?

result.question: Which port gives out the GNSS location data?
result.answer: The GNSS NMEA logs can be fetched using the GNSS_TXD and GNSS_RXD pins [HW-v5.3-p052-1]. Additionally, the module's UART2 serial port, located at pins 22 and 23, is used to obtain GNSS NMEA data [HW-v5.3-p035-1]. Note that UART2 and the GNSS UART are internally connected, so UART2 must be kept floating while using the GNSS interface and vice versa [HW-v5.3-p035-1].

case.question: Can the module send files over FTP?

result.question: Can the module send files over FTP?
result.answer: Yes, the Cavli C16QS module can upload data or local files to a remote side using the AT+CFTPPUT command [AT-v3.1-p144-2]. The maximum data size that can be sent is 20kB [AT-v3.1-p144-2]. Additionally, from firmware version 1.4.1, it is possible to download or store a file up to 120KB [AT-v3.1-p143-1]. Note that file mode in TCP and FTP cannot operate simultaneously [AT-v3.1-p143-1].
